bibl.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We propose an alternative generator architecture for generative adversarial networks, borrowing from style transfer literature.

span.label: latent-space disentanglement in GAN image synthesis
span.quote: There are various definitions for disentanglement [54, 50, 2, 7, 19], but a common goal is a latent space that consists of linear subspaces, each of which controls one factor of variation.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Motivated by style transfer literature [27], we re-design the generator architecture in a way that exposes novel ways to control the image synthesis process.

span.label: the input latent space, constrained to follow the training-data density, has some unavoidable entanglement
span.quote: The input latent space must follow the probability density of the training data, and we argue that this leads to some degree of unavoidable entanglement.

span.label: The perceptual path length measurement is admitted to be biased in favour of the input latent space Z.
span.quote: Yet, this measurement is in fact slightly biased in favor of the input latent space Z.

span.label: Continued FID improvement during training comes at the cost of a more entangled representation (rising path lengths).
span.quote: Even when the training has reached the full 10242 resolution, the slowly rising path lengths indicate that the improvements in FID come at the cost of a more entangled representation.

span.label: The new FFHQ face dataset was crawled from Flickr and therefore inherits that site's biases.
span.quote: (thus inheriting all the biases of that website) and automatically aligned [31] and cropped.

span.label: The central term has no agreed definition and the paper proceeds on a shared goal instead.
span.quote: There are various definitions for disentanglement [54, 50, 2, 7, 19], but a common goal is a latent space that consists of linear subspaces, each of which controls one factor of variation

span.label: The two metrics reported are new because the existing ones cannot be run here, so the numbers compare to nobody.
span.quote: Unfortunately the metrics recently proposed for quantifying disentanglement [26, 32, 7, 19] require an encoder network that maps input images to latent codes

span.label: The perceptual distance the headline metric is built on is another network's embedding, fitted to human ratings.
span.quote: we use a perceptually-based pairwise image distance [65] that is calculated as a weighted difference between two VGG16 [58] embeddings, where the weights are fit so that the metric agrees with human perceptual similarity judgments

span.label: The mechanism claimed for the improvement is posited rather than shown.
span.quote: We posit that there is pressure for the generator to do so, as it should be easier to generate realistic images based on a disentangled representation than based on an entangled representation

span.label: What the paper controls under the name 'style' includes the pose and the shape of the face.
span.quote: Copying the styles corresponding to coarse spatial resolutions (42 – 82) brings high-level aspects such as pose, general hair style, face shape, and eyeglasses from source B

span.label: 'style' - REUSED BY THE AUTHORS' OWN DECISION, FOR ARCHITECTURAL RESEMBLANCE: they say plainly that they choose to reuse the word for the vector y because similar network architectures are already used in feedforward style transfer and image-to-image translation, so the word marks a family of architectures rather than a property of a picture
span.quote: We choose to reuse the word “style” for y because similar network architectures are already used for feedforward style transfer [27], unsupervised image-toimage translation [28], and domain mixtures

span.label: style, once more removed - AS SPATIALLY INVARIANT STATISTICS: the paper's warrant is the style transfer literature's finding that spatially invariant statistics encode style while spatially varying features encode the instance, which is the same move gatys2015 made with a Gram matrix
span.quote: This observation is in line with style transfer literature, where it has been established that spatially invariant statistics (Gram matrix, channel-wise mean, variance, etc.) reliably encode the style of an image [20, 39] while spatially varying features encode a specific instance

span.label: disentanglement - A GOAL STANDING IN FOR A DEFINITION: the paper records that the literature holds various definitions and adopts the shared aim of a latent space of linear subspaces, then measures that aim with two metrics of its own devising
span.quote: There are various definitions for disentanglement [54, 50, 2, 7, 19], but a common goal is a latent space that consists of linear subspaces, each of which controls one factor of variation

span.label: style AT COARSE RESOLUTION - POSE, FACE SHAPE AND EYEGLASSES: the styles copied from the coarse spatial resolutions carry high-level aspects of the subject itself, so at this level the word ranges over what the picture is OF and not only how it looks
span.quote: Copying the styles corresponding to coarse spatial resolutions (42 – 82) brings high-level aspects such as pose, general hair style, face shape, and eyeglasses from source B

span.label: style ON NON-FACE DATASETS - CAMERA VIEWPOINT AND CHOICE OF FURNITURE: in bedrooms the coarse styles control where the camera is and the middle styles select which furniture appears, which an art historian would call composition and subject matter rather than style
span.quote: the coarse styles basically control the viewpoint of the camera, middle styles select the particular furniture, and fine styles deal with colors and smaller details of materials

span.label: builds-on → style transfer literature
span.quote: Motivated by style transfer literature [27], we re-design the generator architecture in a way that exposes novel ways to control the image synthesis process.

span.label: builds-on → Progressive GAN (Karras et al.)
span.quote: Our baseline configuration (A) is the Progressive GAN setup of Karras et al.

span.label: builds-on → the Progressive GAN setup of Karras et al. [30]
span.quote: Our baseline configuration (A) is the Progressive GAN setup of Karras et al. [30], from which we inherit the networks and all hyperparameters except where stated otherwise.

span.label: extends → the parallel self-modulation work of Chen et al. [6]
span.quote: In parallel work, Chen et al. [6] “self modulate” the generator using AdaINs, similarly to our work, but do not consider an intermediate latent space or noise inputs.

span.label: style —operationalised-as→ spatially invariant statistics
span.quote: This observation is in line with style transfer literature, where it has been established that spatially invariant statistics (Gram matrix, channel-wise mean, variance, etc.) reliably encode the style of an image [20, 39] while spatially varying features encode a specific instance

span.label: perceptual path length —distinct-from→ linear separability
span.quote: we propose two new automated metrics — perceptual path length and linear separability — for quantifying these aspects of the generator

span.label: 50,000 — images used to compute the FID metric
span.quote: we calculate the FIDs using 50,000 images drawn randomly

span.label: 1024×1024 — output resolution (progressive from 4x4 to 1024x1024)
span.quote: two for each resolution (42 − 10242)

span.label: standard-deviation
span.quote: (a) Generated image (b) Stochastic variation (c) Standard deviation (a) Two generated Figure 4.
